action: Prefer DOAC over warfarin for anticoagulation in HF with AF
action_detail: For patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients. DOACs do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment, and their fixed dosing with fewer drug-drug interactions simplifies management particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF.

properties.context: preferred over warfarin in HF patients

source_text: For patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients (Class I, LOE A)

action: Warfarin has more drug-drug interactions than DOACs in HF patients on polypharmacy
action_detail: Warfarin requires routine anticoagulation monitoring and dose adjustment, and has more drug-drug interactions compared with DOACs. The polypharmacy commonly seen in HF increases the clinical significance of warfarin interactions. When warfarin is used (due to cost, other indications, or patient factors), clinicians should be aware of interaction potential with other HF medications. DOACs are generally preferred due to fewer interactions.
source_text: The fixed dosing together with fewer interactions may simplify patient management, particularly with the polypharmacy commonly seen in HF...Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions

action: Monitor INR for patients on warfarin with HF and AF
action_detail: Warfarin requires routine anticoagulation monitoring and dose adjustment unlike DOACs. INR monitoring is essential given the drug-drug interaction potential in HF patients on polypharmacy. DOACs do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring.

properties.context: routine anticoagulation monitoring required in HF with AF

source_text: These drugs [DOACs] do not need routine anticoagulation monitoring or dose adjustment...compared with warfarin (Class I, LOE A)

action: Monitor serum digoxin concentration to maintain levels 0.5 to less than 0.9 ng/mL
action_detail: Digoxin serum concentration should be monitored. The risk of death is independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with significantly higher risk observed in those with concentrations >= 1.2 ng/mL and >= 1.6 ng/mL. Target serum digoxin concentration is 0.5 to < 0.9 ng/mL. Drug-drug interactions (e.g., with amiodarone) can increase digoxin levels, making monitoring essential.

action: Anticoagulate HF patients with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc score >= 2 (men) or >= 3 (women)
action_detail: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >= 2 (for men) and >= 3 (for women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy for stroke prevention. This applies regardless of whether patients receive rhythm or rate control.
source_text: Patients with chronic HF with permanent-persistent-paroxysmal AF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of >= 2 (men) and >= 3 (women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy (Class I, LOE A)

action: AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms in HF patients with symptomatic AF
action_detail: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and quality of life. In AATAC trial, ablation improved maintenance of sinus rhythm compared with amiodarone, with 45% decrease in hospitalization and decrease in mortality. In CASTLE AF, the composite endpoint of death or rehospitalization was lower with ablation (28.5%) compared with standard care (44.6%).

properties.context: preferred over amiodarone for rhythm control in HF

source_text: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and QOL (Class IIa, LOE B-R). Ablation versus amiodarone: AATAC showed 45% decrease in hospitalization and decreased mortality

action: Use warfarin instead of DOAC when drug-drug interactions favor warfarin monitoring
action_detail: Anticoagulation may be accomplished with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost, or drug-drug interactions. While DOAC is generally preferred, warfarin may be chosen when its INR monitoring enables safer management of known drug-drug interactions (e.g., with amiodarone, which can be titrated based on INR). This is particularly relevant in HF patients on antiarrhythmics.
source_text: Anticoagulation may be accomplished with DOAC or with warfarin when favored because of other indications, cost or drug-drug interactions (the DOAC are generally preferred)

action: Anticoagulation is reasonable for HF patients with AF even without additional CHA2DS2-VASc risk factors
action_detail: HF is a hypercoagulable state and serves as an independent risk factor for stroke, systemic embolism, and mortality in the setting of AF. In patients with HF and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 1, those with AF had a 3-fold higher risk. The decision to anticoagulate can be individualized according to risk versus benefit. Additional risk factors may not be required to support anticoagulation.
source_text: HF is a hypercoagulable state and serves as an independent risk factor for stroke in AF. In patients with HF and CHA2DS2-VASc of 1, those with AF had 3-fold higher risk (Class IIa, LOE B-NR)
